full_judgment: 2. The short fact leading to this petition is that on 12.2.1992 First Information Report was lodged with Kotwali Police Station, Comilla against Faruque Alamgir and 15/20 unknown persons alleging that they kidnapped one Abdul Bari brother-in-law of the informant at 10:00 P.M. and tried to obtain his signature in some blank papers at a point of Pistol and Pipe-gun which caused blood pressure and said Abdul Bari became senseless and ultimately he was admitted in a clinic and thereafter died on 14.2.1992 at BIRDEM Hospital, Dhaka. On receipt of the First Information Report police took up investigation of the case and ultimately submitted charge sheet against Faruque and Alamgir under sections 143/342/304 of the Penal Code. The accused appellants were not sent up in the charge sheet. On 9.6.1993 the informant filed a Narazi petition with a prayer for taking cognizance against nine persons, which included the accused appellant No.2 Swapan and accused appellant No.3 Md. Nazrul and no prayer was made for taking cognizance against appellant No.1 Abu Bakar. The learned Magistrate after hearing by order dated 26.6.1993 took cognizance against 21 accused persons including the appellants under sections 143/342/304 of the penal Code. The appellants voluntarily surrendered before the learned Sessions Judge, Comilla on 9.10.1993 and were remanded to custody. The appellants along with others preferred Criminal Appeal No. 1129 of 1993 before the learned Sessions Judge, Comilla and prayed for bail which was rejected. They then filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.2004 of 1993 and the appellants were favoured with ad interim bail. Thereafter ad interim bail was recalled by the High Court Division on 17.5.1994 on the ground of misuse of privilege of bail. The appellants before the High Court Division filed counter affidavit denying the allegation of misuse of privilege of bail but the same was not considered at the time of cancellation of ad interim bail. The petitioners filed petition for leave to appeal before this Division against cancellation of ad interim bail but that was not pressed. Then the appellant preferred the present Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1911 of 1994 before the High Court Division for bail, which was rejected. Then the present appeal was filed wherein leave was granted to consider the following: "Mr. Abdul Matin Khasru, learned Advocate appearing with the leave of the court submits that the High Court Division failed to consider two important aspects of the petitioners renewed application for bail first the ad interim bail was earlier cancelled on the ground that the petitioners had beaten up one Abul Hashem a person of the informant's camp on 18.2.1994 after obtaining ad interim bail. The police started F.R. Case No.256 of 1994 on this allegation and it ended in a final repot under Memo No. 181 dated 21.3.1994. The police after proper investigation found the said case as false and fabricated. The State did not put forward any reason for not granting bail to the petitioners in the second Miscellaneous Case.
